title: Definition
text: $$cos\left(\frac{3\pi}{4}\right)$$ is the x-coordinate of the point on the circle that lies along the circumference corresponding to the angle measure $$\frac{3\pi}{4}$$.\n##figure1.gif##

title: $$45-45-90$$ triangle
text: The absolute values of the coordinates of this angle are given by the legs of a triangle with angles of $$45$$, $$45$$, and $$90$$. The hypotenuse has length $$1$$. The x-coordinate and y-coordinate lengths are equal and satisfy the Pythagorean theorem $$1=\sqrt{x^2+x^2}=\sqrt{2x^2}=\sqrt{2} x$$. Thus, the coordinates are both $$\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$$ with signs determined by the location of the angle in the plane.\n##figure2.gif##

title: Coordinate
text: The point on the unit circle with angle $$\frac{3\pi}{4}$$ is in the second quadrant. Thus, the x-coordinate is negative, so it is $$\frac{-1}{\sqrt{2}}$$.\n##figure3.gif##
